tex_content.html:
Corollary
↗ prop:jacobi-fields-vanishing-at-point 1. ch10:10.11

If $U$ is a normal neighborhood of $p$, every vector in $T_qM$ for $q\in U\setminus \{ p\} $ is the value at $q$ of a Jacobi field along a radial geodesic that vanishes at $p$.

Proof

\sketch In normal coordinates write $q=(q^1,\ldots ,q^n)$ and $w=w^i\partial _i|_q$. The radial geodesic $\gamma (t)=(tq^1,\ldots ,tq^n)$ joins $p$ to $q$, and (10.7) gives $J(t)=tw^i\partial _i|_{\gamma (t)}$, with $J(0)=0$ and $J(1)=w$.

□
